findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify and document the exact pipx version and invocation (with or without `--cooldown`) that produces the 'pipx needs uv>=0.9.17' error for a plain source-path install, and update the troubleshooting note's trigger description accordingly so readers know the precise conditions under which the workaround is needed.
evidence: Official pipx docs: '--cooldown DAYS maps to uv's --exclude-newer P{DAYS}D. Relative cooldowns need uv 0.9.17 or newer.' (pipx.pypa.io/latest/how-to/use-uv-backend.html)
The plan does not mention --cooldown, implying the failure arises from a plain `pipx install` invocation, but official docs only tie the uv>=0.9.17 requirement to the cooldown feature.
ABSENCE: The plan does not specify which pipx version the user had installed, which would determine whether a hard minimum-uv-version check exists independently of --cooldown.
findings.finding: The plan states that `pipx install "<path>[agents]"` fails with 'pipx needs uv>=0.9.17 but the host reports 0.7.18' for any plain source install when host uv < 0.9.17. However, per official pipx docs, the uv>=0.9.17 requirement is specifically tied to the `--cooldown DAYS` feature (relative cooldowns), not to plain `pipx install`. A vanilla `pipx install` with the uv backend and uv 0.7.18 would not necessarily produce this exact error unless `--cooldown` is involved or the installed pipx version enforces a hard minimum uv version independent of cooldowns. The plan does not verify which pipx version or which invocation flags the user was running, leaving the stated failure trigger potentially inaccurate, which could mislead readers about when to apply the workaround.
findings.location: Context / Problem section: 'pipx install "<path>[agents]" fails when pipx selects a host uv older than 0.9.17, with an error saying pipx needs uv>=0.9.17 but the host reports 0.7.18'
scenarios: A reader with uv 0.8.x and no cooldown flag tries `pipx install --backend pip` and wonders why it was ever needed — the doc's trigger condition doesn't match their situation.
Future pipx versions that no longer enforce a hard minimum uv for plain installs make the note misleading or create confusion about which versions it applies to.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm with the reporter whether `--cooldown` was being passed or whether their pipx version (e.g., 1.7+) enforces a hard uv minimum independently. Then restate the trigger precisely: e.g., 'pipx versions that use the uv backend and enforce uv>=0.9.17 (e.g., when `--cooldown` is passed, or on pipx>=X.Y with a hard uv minimum)' — or if it truly fires on any plain install with certain pipx versions, note the specific pipx version range.
